title: Span hierarchy flattening proposals (wip)
content:
Summary:
Small exploratory doc collecting proposals for a new interaction model we’re calling "span-hierarchy flattening". Goal: make it easier to scan long waterfalls with deep nested RPC/queue stacks while preserving context and fast access to parent/span metadata. This is a WIP for planning an A/B experiment and a small engineering spike.

Background / problem:
- Long traces (10k+ spans) are hard to scan in the waterfall. Deep nesting pushes relevant sibling spans off-screen.
- Support engineers often want both: (a) a compact, high-density overview for hotspots and (b) the ability to expand into the exact call chain quickly.
- Current fold/unfold UI is binary (collapsed vs full) and not selective enough; users create many manual collapses.
- Prefix/KV caching noise and retry spans create misleading depth.

Design goals:
- Reduce vertical noise while preserving parent-child relationship semantics in a glanceable way.
- Allow lightweight contextual expansion (inline or overlay) without jumping the timeline.
- Keep keyboard-first navigation for power users; gestures for touch/trackpad too.
- Surface sampling/aggregation info (how many spans collapsed, representative child).

Proposal A: Hierarchy flattening by depth banding (safe, incremental)
- Concept: collapse levels > N into a single compact row per parent, with an indicator + summary of top K children (by duration or frequency).
- UI: each collapsed band shows: collapsed-count badge, longest-child label, min/median/max duration sparkline, warning icon if any error/span-exception present.
- Interaction: click on badge -> inline expansion reveals the band (not full trace). Option to "pop out" into focused waterfall panel.
- Defaults: N=3 for desktop, N=2 for narrow view. User control via settings panel per-trace.
- Benefit: low risk, simple to implement by reusing current folding code path, should reduce vertical height for deep traces by ~30–70% depending on distribution.

Proposal B: Density-mode with parent-highlight overlay (experimental)
- Concept: two-layer visual: compressed timeline for all spans (thin rows), and hover/focus highlights reconstruct parent chain in overlay lanes.
- UI: waterfall becomes a compact heatmap (rows = flattened span buckets). Hovering a span or keyboard-selecting it draws connector ribbons up/down to show immediate parent/children in small overlay chips.
- Interaction: spacebar toggles "density mode". Enter opens standard inspector. Right-arrow opens sibling quick-jump.
- Drawbacks: more visual changes, accessibility risk, higher engineering effort (canvas drawing + hit-testing).

Proposal C: Sampling + exemplar extraction (aggregation-first)
- Concept: detect repeated subtree patterns (retries, fan-out, queue loops) and show a single exemplar with a small counter. Allow expanding exemplar to playback the common pattern.
- UI: exemplar row with "n x" tag, small thumbnail timeline, and an action dropdown: expand, inspect exemplar, exclude from view.
- Use cases: surgeries on patterns, e.g., database reconnection storms, retry loops.

Interaction primitives (shared across proposals)
- Inline expansion vs overlay detail: prefer inline for small bands, overlay (floating panel) for deep/large expansions so time axis doesn’t reflow too much.
- Keyboard: j/k to move selection, o to open compact inspector, e to expand/contract collapsed band, shift+o to open expanded overlay.
- Mouse: hover preview card with top-3 tags, click-to-expand on collapsed badge, right-click > jump-to-parent.
- Touch: long-press for preview, drag-to-expand for consecutive bands.

Wireframe sketches (text):
- Collapsed band row example:
  [parent-span]  [child1-summary | child2-summary | child3-summary]  [···]  [badge: 42]  [sparkline: ▂▅▇▅▂]  [err⚠]
- Density heatmap example:
  [time axis]
  row1 ░░░██░░░  (service-a)
  row2 ░░░░░█░░  (service-b)
  row3 ░█████░░  (queue/retry blocks)
  hover -> overlay: parent chain lanes draw small chips with vertical connectors

Acceptance criteria (for MVP experiment):
- Reduction in median trace vertical height for traces > 500 spans by >= 40% for Proposal A.
- No regression in time-to-inspect (measured as time from open to first subset-expansion action) for power users (j/k/enter flows) - target < 3s median.
- No accessibility score regression (a11y automated checks).
- User feedback NPS on readability improves vs control (qual surveys in experiment).

Metrics to collect:
- vertical_px_saved_per_trace (derived), collapsed_rows_count, expand_action_rate, popout_overlay_open_rate, keyboard_navigation_fraction, time_to_first_action, trace_inspection_success_rate (from support ticket tagging).

Experiment plan (phases):
1) Spike (2w): implement Proposal A as server-side collapse + client renders collapsed rows. Minimal UI polish.
   - Owner: Evan (front-end), Marco (runtime/proxy collapse flags), Priya (spec/metrics).
2) Internal dogfood (1w): product+SRE use on internal traces. Collect metrics, iterate.
3) A/B test (3w): 10% of users get flattened view; measure metrics above.
4) Decide ship / iterate.

Backlog (rough):
- Frontend: collapsed band renderer, badge interactions, inline expansion animation (5d)
- Backend: collapsed-band summary aggregator (map-reduce style) (4d)
- Telemetry: instrumentation for new metrics (2d)
- UX: microcopy, settings toggle, keyboard mapping (2d)
- QA: stress traces, a11y audit, perf (3d)
- Docs: release notes + admin toggle (1d)

Open questions / risks:
- How to pick "representative" child? duration vs error vs frequency — need heuristics and possibly a user preference.
- Is reflow on expansion disruptive for users reading the time axis? Overlay mitigates but adds complexity.
- How will rollouts interact with Dedicated/private (latency of summarization)? We should do summarization client-side first to reduce infra changes.
- Edge case: traces with many short parallel children (fan-out) — flattened band might hide concurrency. Need a small concurrency glyph.

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- Could combine with span-sampling flag in profiling API and return a "collapse token" for heavy subtrees; client can request expansion by token.
- Consider small "peek on hover" that shows top 5 spans of collapsed band in a compact vertical rail.
- Add a small config: "flatten depth" and "show concurrency glyphs" in trace settings menu (persist per-user).

Links to related drive drafts:
- see: shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/trace-session-playback-and-snapshotting-grooming.json (for popout patterns)
- see: shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/waterfall-interaction-edge-cases-accessibility-draft.json (accessibility checklist)

Next steps (this week):
- Evan: drop a frontend POC branch with collapsed rows (end of week) -> link back here.
- Marco: sketch quick aggregator endpoint (proto) and perf budget estimate.
- Priya: draft microcopy and experiment survey questions.

Unresolved UX decisions (to discuss Tues):
- Inline expansion animation type: push content vs overlay. pros/cons table.
- Default depth threshold (N). propose N=3 but want data-driven choice.

Quotable for PRD later: "Flattened bands let you skim a thousand-span trace in the time it takes to skim three screenfuls—without losing the ability to replay exact call chains."

End notes: this doc intentionally light on visuals — next iteration will paste Figma frames and simple screenshot POCs.
